chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Amr ibn Hilal, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of directing your gaze towards those who are above you in wealth, and suffice with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)':
Let not their property and their children astound you
And He said: 'And do not stretch your eyes after that with which We have provided wedded pairs of them, blossoms of the life of the world.'

So if anything from that enters into you, then remember the life of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), for indeed his provision was barley, his sweetener was dates, and his fuel was palm stalks when he found them.

key_terms.زَهْرَةَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا: Blossoms of the life of the world

ai.seo_question: How to cure envy of wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) advises against envying the worldly wealth and children of others, citing Quranic verses to suffice the heart. He recommends remembering the simple, ascetic lifestyle of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) as a remedy for worldly attachment.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ammar Bin Marwan, from Zay Bin Al Shahham, from Amro Bin Hilal who said,

Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Beware of aspiring your vision towards the one who is above you, and suffice with what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Said to His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>
[9:55] Let not then their property and their children astound you.
And Heazwj Said [20:131] And do not stretch your eyes after that with which We have Provided wedded pairs of them, blossoms of the life of the world.

So if anything from that enters into you, then remember the life of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, So rather, his<sup>asws</sup> provision was the barley and the sweetness of the dates, and his<sup>saww</sup> fuel was the firewood, when he<sup>saww</sup> found it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan from Zayd al-Shahham from ‘Amr ibn Hilal who has said the following:

“I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘You must never allow your eyes aim for one who is above you (in worldly matters that may tempt you wish for his opportunity). The words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, to His Messenger are enough evidence to support it.
“Let not their property and children tempt you. . . .” [9:55]
‘Do not yearn for other people’s property and wives and do not grieve. . . .’ [15:88]
If you sense such a feeling then consider the life of the Messenger of Allah. He lived on barley loaves and sweetness from dates. For fuel he would use palm tree twigs if he could find them.”’
